## I. CONTEXT

The province of Ituri is situated in the north-east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and shares a long border with Uganda and South Sudan.
For more than two decades, it has been confronted with a chronic humanitarian crisis linked to armed conflicts and recurrent population displacements.
It has an estimated population of more than 8 million inhabitants, among whom are more than one million internally displaced persons.

In September 2018, this province was affected by an outbreak of Ebola virus disease that was raging in the neighbouring province of Nord-Kivu.

The health zone of Mongbwalu is one of the 36 health zones of the province of Ituri.
Considered the starting point of the epidemic, it is situated in the territory of Djugu where several armed groups operate.
It is situated 70 km from Bunia, the capital of Ituri province, with frequent population movements towards Uganda.
This locality has the particularity of having several mining/construction sites that attract populations coming from other territories of the province and neighbouring provinces.

## II. OUTBREAK HISTORY

On 05 May 2026, social media declared an outbreak of deaths of unknown cause with nearly 50 deaths already recorded in the Mongbwalu health zone.
Following confirmation of this alert, the Chief Medical Officer of the Mongbwalu health zone shared the preliminary investigation report on 09 May 2026.
On 11 May 2026, provincial health authorities organised an emergency meeting and decided to deploy rapid response teams to Mongbwalu and Rwampara, which had reported suspected viral haemorrhagic fever deaths among patients admitted to the Evangelical Medical Centre of Rwampara, coming from Mongbwalu.

Investigations conducted on 12 May 2026 simultaneously in the Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones by the Rapid Intervention Teams of the Provincial Health Division (DPS) of Ituri showed that most suspected patients or deaths presented with fever, headache, vomiting, and intense physical asthenia.
Deaths occurred 2 to 3 days after disease onset with haematemesis, epistaxis or blackish vomiting.
During investigations in the Rwampara health zone, 20 samples from suspected cases or deaths were collected.
The majority of persons sampled came from the Mongbwalu health zone.
Preliminary tests conducted at the Bunia Laboratory were all negative for Ebola Zaire, dengue, Rotavirus, Cholera, Malaria, Yersinia pestis, mpox and COVID-19.
These samples were sent to the National Institute of Biomedical Research (INRB) in Kinshasa for additional testing.

On 14 May 2026, 13 of these 20 samples were tested and 8 were positive for non-Zaire Ebola virus disease at INRB Kinshasa.
On 15 May 2026, sequencing of the positive samples identified the BUNDIBUGYO strain, which enabled the Minister of Public Health, Hygiene and Social Welfare (MSHPS) to officially declare the 17th outbreak of Ebola virus disease.
Ebola virus disease (Bundibugyo strain), thus marking the 17th epidemic in the country's history

On 17 May 2026, in consultation with member states, the Director-General of WHO deemed that the event occurring in DRC and Uganda met the definition criteria set out in Article 1 of the IHR, and declared that this constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern while specifying that the risk at the global level is low but high at the regional level.

On 18 May 2026, the Director General of Africa CDC officially declared a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3 of its statutes.
This declaration followed an emergency meeting of the Africa CDC advisory group, which considered that the worsening outbreak constituted an acute risk to continental health security.
Consequently, the continental incident management support team was activated to provide support to affected member states and those exposed to risks, in response and preparedness.

## II. EPIDEMIOLOGICAL SITUATION UPDATE

Thirteen (13) new confirmed cases, including 1 case in Nord-Kivu (Katwa ZS (health zone)) and 12 in Ituri (Rwampara: 3, Bunia: 5, Nyakunde: 3 and Bambu: 1).
One new zone affected in Ituri province, namely Bambu.
Cumulative confirmed cases stand at 64 cases, including 60 in DPS Ituri (8 ZS affected) and 4 in Nord-Kivu (3 ZS affected).
Listing of 414 new contacts, including 286 in Rwampara ZS and 128 in Bambu ZS.
No new confirmed deaths.
Cumulative deaths stand at 6, including 2 in Nord-Kivu and 4 in Ituri.

## III. RESPONSE ACTIONS

### COORDINATION

• Holding of a coordination meeting chaired by the Deputy Incident Manager, Head of the Provincial Health Division of Nord-Kivu (Beni) and Ituri (Bunia).
• Holding of a partner mobilisation meeting on alignment with the response plan.
• Drafting of the provincial operational plan for the Ebola Virus Disease incident in DPS Ituri and Nord-Kivu.

### EPIDEMIOLOGICAL SURVEILLANCE

Support to Katwa and Goma ZS in in-depth investigation and contact listing around confirmed cases.
Setting up of an alert management system (popularisation of the civil protection toll-free number).
Start of contact tracing around the confirmed case in Goma ZS and ongoing activation in the Ituri ZS.
Alert note from the corresponding PoE in Ntoronko/Uganda regarding the risk of contamination from Congolese residents in Uganda returning from mourning ceremonies for their deceased relatives in DRC on the shores of Lake Albert.
In-depth investigations and contact listing around 4 confirmed cases in Nord Kivu and 58 cases in Ituri.

Identification of resources by PoE/PoC (124 providers for 10 PoC).
Provision of 120 plastic chairs, 60 boxes of gloves and other PCI (infection prevention and control) materials (liquid soaps, etc.) by IOM.
Assessment of the Kasindi and Nobili PoE and evaluation of the Eringeti, Mavivi Airport, PK5 and Nzuma PoC.

### RISK COMMUNICATION AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT (RCCE)

• Broadcast of the Provincial Military Governor's message on compliance with control measures against the Communication plan currently being drafted
• Production of provisional communication timetables
• Production of two official messages, one for preparedness and the other for response
• Communication session for provincial government executives and staff during morning parade;
• Briefing of Presicodesa on strengthening SBC, RCCE, alert reporting and community feedback collection;
• Holding of the first meeting to analyse rumours and community feedback.
• Advocacy with the Mayor of the City of Bunia to prohibit the organisation of funeral wakes during this MVE (Ebola virus disease) response period
• Advocacy with the EPST Bunia Sub-Proved to relay the PROVED instruction prohibiting sending pupils home for not wearing a mask.
• Advocacy with the Commander of the Régie des Voies Aériennes (RVA) of Bunia

### INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL

Bunia ZS
▪ 2 EDS completed and 1 ongoing;
▪ Briefing of 5 healthcare providers from the HGR (general referral hospital)-Bunia emergency room on preventive measures;
▪ Provision of PPE and decontamination equipment for the practical session of the Bunia ZS teams;
▪ Decontamination of the isolation building at HGR-Bunia.
▪ Provision of some PCI supplies by partner ALIMA

Rwampara ZS
▪ Briefing of 4 staff from the BALIDJA Mortuary on wearing PPE before handling any body;
▪ Continuation of briefing of 63 healthcare providers (Hygienists, nurses, Doctors and Midwives) from CME Nyakunde) on biomedical waste management.
▪ 3 EDS completed and 1 ongoing
▪ Decontamination of the isolation room at HGR/Rwampara;
▪ Briefing of 10 cleaners and 15 PCI supervisors on donning and doffing PPE.

Mongbwalu ZS
▪ Supportive supervision in 4 health facilities, namely: CS Uponyaji, CS Rwampara, Amani Health Post and CS Tchunga (without conducting evaluation);

DPS Nord Kivu
• Decontamination of Matanda Hospital where the confirmed case from Katwa ZS is staying;
• PCI score card evaluation of Matanda Hospital: 70,6%;
• Performance of case mapping;
• Assessment of the CTE (Ebola treatment centre) to identify needs for PCI supplies (PPE, water supply, waste management, patient circuit).

• Preparation of the logistics statement of needs for the ZS of Goma, Katwa, Beni, Karisimbi, Mutwanga, Vuhovi, Kalunguta, Kamango, Mabalako, Oicha, Museniene, Kayina, Alimbongo, Butembo;
• Procurement of Starlink kits for internet connectivity from UNICEF;
• Receipt of 5 vehicles donated by WHO;
• Receipt of 200 litres of diesel (Support from MEMISA-Belgium).

• 14 disclosure of results;
• Sensitisation of 97 family carers, 9 hygienists, 11 workers, 92 teachers from CSJM and 25 taxi drivers;
• Family discussion with 4 families of deceased persons;

### SECURITY

• The security situation in the city of Bunia (Bunia and Rwampara ZS) is relatively calm
• Security briefing to deployed teams.

## III. CHALLENGES

Lack of standard CT (transit centre) and CTE
Shortage of PCI materials (PPE, handwashing stations, chlorine) in Nord Kivu
Low reporting of alerts by zones;
Insufficient financial resources to support all response pillars;
Difficulty transporting samples to laboratories in Goma and Kinshasa.
Spread of rumours and proliferation of traditional treatment remedies.
Lack of communication materials and tools.
Lack of office supplies and equipment (IT equipment);
Insufficient vehicles for team movement in the field;

## VI. Recommendation

Make operational the CT and CTE in Beni, Butembo and Goma (rehabilitation and circuit revision)
Strengthen surveillance to enhance alert reporting and tracing of contacts never seen and lost to follow-up;
Mobilise resources to support the different pillars of the response;
Strengthen analysis of rumours and community feedback and carry out actions to address them
Supply communication materials and tools
